clue.text: Building we put in high place?

indicators.note: put in tells us the word we is placed inside the word for a high place

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hilltop, a high place

explanation.surface: A question about which lofty spot we should choose for our new building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' places the pronoun inside the hilltop word, splitting it after its second letter; a tor is a rocky peak found on English moors.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure such as a church steeple or castle keep is a building in its own right.

clue.text: Coach, perhaps, or team-leader, organized game

parts.note: the leading letter of the word team
ran means managed or organized, as in ran the show
a sport is a game

explanation.surface: Choosing a coach, or a captain to organise the match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' tempts as a sports trainer; here it is a bus, an example of the definition, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a long-distance bus, one example of a means of conveying passengers.

clue.text: Author wanting extra Line inserted

indicators.note: inserted means the letter for line is put into the word for extra

parts.note: in cricket a wide is one of the extras, runs not scored off the bat

explanation.surface: A writer needing an additional line added to the script.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is an extra run conceded when a ball is bowled out of reach.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish wit who wrote The Importance of Being Earnest was a playwright and author.

clue.text: Convoluted procedure to fix a part after month

indicators.note: after means the part follows the month

parts.note: to rig is to fix fraudulently
a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A tiresome process for arranging a part after waiting a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts A ROLE after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, complicated and tedious process or rambling story is a palaver.

clue.text: Making fun of absurd racialist

indicators.note: absurd suggests the letters of racialist are made nonsense of and rearranged

explanation.surface: Mocking someone who holds ridiculous racist views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absurd' looks like a description of the racialist but signals the anagram of RACIALIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire is mockery, so a mocking piece of writing is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Bottom number to submit is being raised

indicators.note: being raised in a down clue says the pieces read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to put a question or proposal is to submit it

explanation.surface: A count of buttocks offered up for inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being raised' reverses the whole run NO PUT IS in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, the part of the body you sit on is the rear, the backside.

clue.text: Story I'm rewriting the right way?

indicators.note: rewriting means the letters of story I'm are written out again in a new order

explanation.surface: A tale rewritten in a conservative manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewriting' shuffles STORY IM; 'right' refers to the political right, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservative politics belongs to the right wing, so its doctrine is a right-leaning way of thinking.

clue.text: Immoveably fix king with one check

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king
I is the Roman numeral one
to vet is to check thoroughly

explanation.surface: Firmly securing a chess king while giving check.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'Immoveably'. R is rex, the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something with a metal bolt so it cannot move, or to hold attention firmly.

clue.text: Main area in centre of new Barbican complex

indicators.note: complex suggests the letters are tangled into a new arrangement
centre of picks out the middle letter of the word new

explanation.surface: An area at the heart of the newly built Barbican development in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbican is a London arts complex. 'centre of' gives E from 'new'; 'complex' rearranges E plus BARBICAN. The Spanish Main was the old name for this sea region.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means the open sea, and this sea area between the Americas was the Spanish Main.

clue.text: European river rising in the French interior

indicators.note: interior says the reversed river goes into the inside of the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the river is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A continental river that rises in the heart of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European river' looks like the definition, but 'river' is the Spanish word that 'rising' turns upwards, and 'interior' sets it inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in France flows through the continent, so it is a waterway of Europe.

clue.text: A gorilla, tame initially, can become a dangerous creature

indicators.note: can become signals the letters turning into something new, a rearrangement
initially means take the first letter of the word tame

explanation.surface: Even a tamed gorilla might turn into something dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan prints 'tame', not 'came'. 'initially' gives T from 'tame'; 'can become' rearranges A GORILLA plus T.
explanation.definitionFit: This large reptile with powerful jaws, a relative of the crocodile, is a hazardous animal.

clue.text: Opera producer needs clever diva in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer looking for a talented soprano for his production.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'needs', which is a link word: the definition that can stand in for the answer is just 'Opera producer'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian who wrote Aida and La Traviata produced many operas, so he is a composer of them.

clue.text: City given another name when it's burnt

definitions.text: City given another name when it's burnt

parts.words: City given another name when it's burnt
parts.note: an Italian city in Tuscany shares its name with an earth pigment; roasted, that pigment is a reddish-brown paint with the word burnt in front

explanation.surface: A city that gets renamed after it is set on fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Burnt sienna is an artist's brown pigment, named after the Tuscan city; the city's spelling has one N.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tuscan city famous for its Palio horse race, whose name with an extra N labels an earth pigment.

clue.text: Right to go in a volume, and good enough

definitions.text: Right to go in a volume, and good enough

indicators.note: to go in means the letter for right is put inside the measure

parts.note: a pint is a measure of volume
able means competent, good enough for the task

explanation.surface: Something fit and suitable to be put into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: something fit to go in a book is suitable for publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Material fit for publication is suitable and decent enough to appear in a book.

clue.text: In error, put on old hat

parts.note: out can mean mistaken, as in a calculation being out
clothes put on are worn

explanation.surface: Someone mistakenly wearing an ancient hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like a garment but is the idiom for stale and unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hackneyed and stale through overuse is described with this adjective, as is old hat.

clue.text: Speculator seeing article on upturn in gold

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the article on top of the rest

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: in means the upturn goes inside the gold

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
an upturn is a rise

explanation.surface: An investor watching an article about gold prices going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as a heraldic tincture is a crossword staple; 'in' puts the upturn inside it, and 'on' stacks the article above in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms hypotheses rather than facts is a speculative thinker.

clue.text: Part of the US that is entered by wife on motorway

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

indicators.note: entered by means the letter for wife goes inside the Latin phrase

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: Describing an American region reached when a wife drives along a highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' is the Latin phrase behind the abbreviation i.e.; 'entered by' puts the wife inside it, and 'on' sets it after the motorway letter, as on the M1 in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The central northern states such as Ohio and Illinois form this region of America.

clue.text: Audacious raid's ending over a Communist base

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the first pieces above the later ones
ending means the final letter of the word raid

parts.note: a red is a communist
base means low and wicked

explanation.surface: A bold raid that brings down a Communist stronghold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a military camp but means morally low.
explanation.definitionFit: A recklessly bold person, or describing one, ready to take wild risks.

clue.text: A distant county, going by air

definitions.text: A distant county, going by air

parts.words: A distant county, going by air
parts.note: an Irish county that a famous First World War marching song says is a long way off; the song is the air it goes by

explanation.surface: A remote county reached by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: A First World War marching song says this Irish county is a long way off; 'air' means tune, not flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish county is celebrated in a song as far away, so it is distant by the tune.

clue.text: Academic writings_about top-class classical hero

indicators.note: about means the academic writings go around the letter for top-class

parts.note: theses are dissertations written for degrees
U means upper-class, top-class, in British usage

explanation.surface: Scholarly papers written about a first-rate ancient Greek hero.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class usage; THESES wraps round it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Athenian slayer of the Minotaur is a hero of Greek myth.

clue.text: Makes an effort to keep king in Cornish town

indicators.note: to keep means the town holds the letter for king inside it

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Trying hard to keep a monarch in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying hard means exerting oneself, which is the same as attempting with effort.

clue.text: This vegetable's a bargain, on average

indicators.note: on means the bargain comes after the average in this across clue

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
a snip is a bargain in British slang

explanation.surface: Boasting that a vegetable was reasonably priced on the whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sends the bargain after the average; snip is British slang for something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale root eaten roasted, related to the carrot, is a kind of vegetable.

clue.text: Pain after pain I ignored in flamboyant style

indicators.note: after means the first pain comes after the second in the answer
ignored means the letter I is dropped from the word pain

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Suffering one pain after another, yet carrying it off with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I ignored' strips the letter I from the first pain, and 'after' places the second pain behind what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dash and swagger in doing things is a flamboyant manner or flair.

clue.text: Settler on a horse

parts.note: a percher is one who settles or alights on a perch
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pioneer riding horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist, but it is one who perches, as a bird settles.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy French draught breed from the Perche region is a type of horse.

clue.text: Chairperson's accepting nothing as conclusive evidence

indicators.note: accepting means the professor takes the zero inside

parts.note: a prof holds a university chair, so is a chairperson
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A committee chair accepting nil as decisive evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairperson' suggests a committee head; here it is a professor holding an academic chair.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence that establishes a fact beyond doubt is demonstration of it.

clue.text: Englishman who put together an astronomical score

definitions.text: Englishman who put together an astronomical score

parts.words: Englishman who put together an astronomical score
parts.note: an English composer who wrote an orchestral suite on the planets of the solar system

explanation.surface: An Englishman who amassed a huge total.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astronomical score' looks like a huge total; it is music about the planets, The Planets suite.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav, the English composer of The Planets, wrote an orchestral score about the heavens.

clue.text: Editor backed rival author

indicators.note: backed means the abbreviation for editor is turned round

parts.note: a foe is an enemy or rival

explanation.surface: An editor supporting a competing writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like support but reverses ED to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: The writer of Robinson Crusoe was an English novelist and author.

clue.text: Raid unceasingly

definitions.meaning: a sudden incursion or sortie into enemy territory
an old phrase meaning for ever, always

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, the second sense is the archaic phrase meaning for aye, for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a sudden attack, and the archaic phrase for ay means eternally.

clue.text: Bird seen where river meets lake

parts.note: the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A bird spotted at the confluence of a river and a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the blackbird, or the water dipper, so a kind of thrush-like bird.

clue.text: Opposing reform of a service? Just the opposite

parts.note: V stands for versus, meaning against or opposing

indicators.note: reform of means the letters of a service are re-formed into a new order

explanation.surface: Opposing church reform? No, quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform of' rearranges A SERVICE into ICEVERSA after V for versus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means the other way round, with the order of things reversed.

clue.text: Early experience providing warning? Not a lot

parts.note: fore is the golfer's shout warning of a ball in flight
a taste is a small amount, not a lot

explanation.surface: A small sample given as a warning of what is to come.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the warning cry on a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sample of something before it fully happens is an advance experience of it.

clue.text: Set aside a place for the rest of the travellers

definitions.meaning: to save or put away for later

definitions.text: a place for the rest of the travellers
definitions.meaning: a roadside parking area where drivers stop for a break

explanation.surface: Reserving a spot where weary travellers can rest.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the second sense is a pull-in beside a road where drivers can stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To save something for later is to put it by, and a roadside pull-in lets drivers stop and rest.
